title: Hatami pseudo-junta approximation
statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, every Boolean-valued function $f$ on its outcome space, and all $K,\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ with $K\ge0$, total influence $I(f)\le K$, and $\varepsilon>0$, there is a Boolean-valued function $h$ on the same space that is a $\exp(CK^3/\varepsilon^3)$-pseudo-junta and satisfies $\Pr_P(f\ne h)\le\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with positive atom weights summing to one in each coordinate
replaced: There is an absolute $C>0$ such that for every product $P$ of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, every $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$, $K\ge0$ with $I(f)\le K$, and $\varepsilon>0$, there is $h:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ with $\Pr_P(f\ne h)\le\varepsilon$ that is determined by locally triggered coordinate observations exposing at most $\exp(CK^3/\varepsilon^3)$ coordinates in expectation.
